newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY LEAGUE-ST HELENS MASTER KICKING GAME TO WIN CUP.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-ST HELENS MASTER KICKING GAME TO WIN CUP.

text.p: Holders St Helens mastered the kicking game to overcome Bradford 32-22 and lift the Challenge Cup English rugby league title at Wembley on Saturday.
Three of five St Helens tries came from kicking moves and captain Bobbie Goulding kicked six goals from seven attempts for a personal tally of 12 points.
The final was delayed 20 minutes by a bomb scare.
Stand-off Tommy Martyn and Goulding combined to score Saints' opening two tries in identical circumstances. Goulding speared low kicks into the goal area and Martyn was on hand to touch down.
Bradford kept pace with their rivals thanks to tries by Danny Peacock and centre Paul Loughlin and 12 minutes before the break the score was locked at 10-10.
Karle Hammond put Saints ahead seconds before halftime when he wrestled his way past five tacklers and Goulding's conversion gave his side a 16-10 lead.
Saints opened a 12-point break eight minutes into the second half when Chris Joynt raced over and Goulding converted.
Luck was on the side of St Helens two minutes later when Anthony Sullivan chased down a kick and was awarded a try although television replays showed he failed to ground the ball cleanly.
Goulding's conversion and a penalty 11 minutes later all but sealed the title for St Helens as they extended their lead to 30-10 with 18 minutes left.
Bradford scored late tries through Glen Tomlinson and James Lowes for the full-time score of 32-22.
